newsitem.title: DENMARK: ISS sees export growth for care service.
newsitem.headline: ISS sees export growth for care service.

text.p: Danish cleaning group International Service System (ISS), eager to expand its care services for the elderly throughout the Nordic region, said on Friday it saw turnover in Sweden increasing steadily.
"We expect growth in Sweden of at least 10 million (Swedish) crowns every year now," ISS Scandinavia managing director Sven Ipsen told Reuters in an interview.

"We have more new contracts coming in, we are optimistic about the way the Swedish market is developing," he said, adding that turnover in Sweden had grown to 220 million Swedish crowns over the 12 months to date from 30 million crowns in 1995.
He said ISS was now the third biggest provider of care for the elderly in Sweden, where such services had been privatised by 40 percent of local authorities over the past seven years.
Ipsen estimated that the Swedish elderly care market had a potential annual turnover of 50 billion crowns, and Denmark, Norway and Finland's were worth 30 billion crowns each.
He said that ISS was also currently looking into developing child care services in the Nordic region, which he saw as a market potentially as large as looking after the aged.
"The most important thing is how big a chunk we can win," Ipsen said.

He said that Sweden was the clear front-runner in privatising care services in the Nordic region, while Denmark, Norway and Finland had so far only farmed out a very small part of their health services to the private sector.
ISS is to enter the Norwegian elderly care market this summer, taking over the running of a home there, but was still mulling whether to go into the field in Finland, Ipsen said.
In Denmark ISS is currently discussing a service concept for running privatised homes for the elderly with seven local authorities.
